overall: Committee violated the law by the chair not stating the executive session purpose or reconvening plan, by vague executive session notice, and by a late location change without reasonable notice; no violation on scope of discussion.

allegations.summary: Chair did not announce whether the committee would reconvene in open session after the April 17 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The Law is clear that the chair must publicly announce during the open session whether the public body will reconvene in open session.

allegations.summary: Chair failed to state the purpose of the April 17 executive session before the motion to enter it was voted.
allegations.key_passage: Because the chair failed to state the purpose of the executive session, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Executive session notice cited the criminal misconduct purpose but did not describe the subject, a ransomware or cybersecurity incident, so it was not specific enough.
allegations.key_passage: We find that by failing to include in the notice a description of the subject to be discussed in executive session, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly deliberated and voted on topics outside the stated executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Having reviewed the executive session minutes in camera, we are satisfied that the Committee’s discussions and votes fell within the stated purpose of the April 17 executive session.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly changed the meeting location less than 48 hours before the meeting without adequate notice to the public.
allegations.key_passage: Because we have been presented with no information suggesting that the Committee made a reasonable effort to notify the public of the new meeting location, we find that it violated the Open Meeting Law when it changed the location of the meeting less than 48 hours prior to the meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
